Type round-tripping is done by a tagging serializer that the default session interface hands to the cookie signer.

**`src/tessel/sessions.py`**
- `SignedCookieSessionInterface` (line 284) is the default session interface. Its `serializer` attribute is `session_json_serializer = TypedCookieSerializer()` (lines 273 and 300), and it passes that serializer to the signing serializer (line 316).
- `SignedCookieSession` (line 57) is the dict-like session object that holds the data.

**`src/tessel/json/tag.py`**
- `TypedCookieSerializer` (line 219) walks the data on the way out with `tag()`. On the way in it restores values with `untag()`, using the registered tag classes.
- `TypeMarker` (line 60) is the base class for the tags. Each subclass checks whether it applies to a value, converts the value to a JSON-safe form wrapped under a one-key marker such as `" t"`, and converts it back.
- `TagTuple` (line 133) handles tuples. It stores them as lists and restores the tuple.
- `TagBytes` (line 159) handles bytes. It base64-encodes them.
- `TagDateTime` (line 205) handles datetimes. It stores them as an HTTP date string and parses it back with `parse_date`.
- `TagDict` (line 93) escapes user dicts whose single key collides with a tag marker.
- `PassDict` (line 119) and `PassList` (line 147) recurse into dicts and lists so nested values get tagged too.
- `TagMarkup` (line 173) and `TagUUID` (line 191) cover `Markup` and `UUID` the same way.
